refused_program.body:
# Refresh the upstream remote-tracking ref that the merge is based on.
git fetch {upstream_remote} {upstream_branch}

# Merge upstream. A clean merge is committed by git itself and we are done.
if git merge --no-edit {upstream_remote}/{upstream_branch}; then
  exit 0
fi

# Keep the local side of each conflicted file and fold in what upstream
# added, by unioning the three index stages (base, ours, theirs) of the
# conflict. Lines the local side deleted stay deleted, since those hunks
# are not in conflict and are already applied.
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
for path in $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U); do
  ours="$tmp/ours"
  base="$tmp/base"
  theirs="$tmp/theirs"
  : > "$ours"
  : > "$base"
  : > "$theirs"
  if ! git show ":2:$path" > "$ours" 2>/dev/null; then
    # Local side deleted this file: keep the deletion.
    git rm -q -f -- "$path"
    continue
  fi
  if ! git show ":3:$path" > "$theirs" 2>/dev/null; then
    # Upstream deleted this file while local changed it: keep ours.
    git add -- "$path"
    continue
  fi
  git show ":1:$path" > "$base" 2>/dev/null || : > "$base"
  git merge-file --union "$ours" "$base" "$theirs" || true
  cp "$ours" "$path"
  git add -- "$path"
done
rm -rf "$tmp"

# Record the merge now that every conflict has been resolved.
if [ -e "$(git rev-parse --git-dir)/MERGE_HEAD" ]; then
  git commit --no-edit
fi
